"The Atlas of Voices": thousands of recordings to draw the map of Arabic dialects. A group of researchers from different Arabic universities launched a digital project called "The Atlas of Voices," which invites volunteers to record short sentences in their local dialects and upload them on a dedicated website. So far, the project has collected more than 20,000 recordings from eighteen countries. The project coordinator explains that the objective "is not to classify dialects or judge them, but to document them before they change," specifying that dialects "move quickly" due to migration, media and social networks. The first maps, he adds, showed between the dialects "soft borders," not separation lines: "There may be no difference between two nearby cities, while between the two ends of the Arab world there are almost different languages." The project protects the confidentiality of participants: no specific names or places of residence are published, but only the region. Each participant may also ask at any time for the cancellation of their registration. Researchers hope that the atlas will be useful to teachers and translators and help change a widespread idea, which sees in dialects a "fuṣḥā Corrupted" while they are, according to the coordinator, "living tongues, with their rules." 11 · Example (speaking) 3):
